ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC rules of every director, UBO, signatory and agent against the federal consolidated Canadian sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list (due to USD clearing), and domestic and foreign politically exposed persons lists. Enhanced due diligence is required for foreign PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and cross-border remittance corridors. Continuous transaction monitoring, suspicious transaction reporting to FINTRAC, and 10-year record retention are mandatory for licensed money services businesses.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: British Columbia Corporate Registry – Corporate Online (OneStop Business Registry) at registriesonline.gov.bc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name must include the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Company' or the abbreviation 'ULC' or 'U.L.C.'; the name must be in the Latin alphabet, English or French; non-Latin script names require certified transliteration or a bilingual English/French form; names must be distinctive, not misleading, and must not imitate a government or regulated financial institution.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may submit a written request for reconsideration to the British Columbia Corporate Registry within 30 calendar days of the rejection decision, attaching the original name request, the legal element, supporting evidence of licensing or consent, and any amended distinctive element. If the rejection is upheld, a new name request may be filed with a revised name; the rejection fee is non-refundable. Further review is available through the Director of Corporate Registry, with judicial review to the Supreme Court of British Columbia in cases of procedural error.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only as the statutory registered office if held by a BC-registered agent with a physical street address and a human agent accepting service. A virtual mailbox cannot satisfy the Money Services Act place-of-business requirement or FINTRAC MSB substance expectations for a licensed remittance agency; a substantive operating office and managerial presence in BC are required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 80% in the first 12 months if licensed as a money services business, given FINTRAC and Consumer Protection BC on-site compliance examinations and surprise inspections; approximately 20% for a non-trading holding ULC with no occupational premises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 10-12, 27, 51, 54; Business Corporations Regulation, BC Reg 2004/288, Part 2
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Registry Services, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Victoria, BC
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) and Notice of Articles (Form 2) submitted under sections 12 and 28 of the Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required; shares may be issued for no par value. No escrow account mandated. ULC is an unlimited liability company; shareholders remain jointly and severally liable with the company for its liabilities under s. 51.2 of the BC Business Corporations Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) The incorporator's subscription for 100 common shares without par value at a subscription price of CAN $1.00 per share be and is hereby accepted; (2) the registered office of the Company be established at [Suite 1000, 123 Main Street, Vancouver, British Columbia V6B 1A1], and the registered and records office shall be maintained at that address; (3) [Full Name] be appointed as the sole director and as Chief Compliance Officer; (4) [Full Name] be appointed as President and [Full Name] as Secretary; (5) all authorized officers are delegated authority to open bank accounts with a Schedule I Canadian bank for payment rail settlement; (6) the Company apply for all applicable money services business registrations and business licenses; and (7) these resolutions be effective upon incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Online (BC Registries and Online Services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) search for the proposed ULC name. File a name reservation application online via BC Registry Online. The name must contain the expression 'U.L.C.' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation'.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is refused or confusing, amend the request with a revised corporate name and resubmit within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the Incorporation Application (Form 1) and Notice of Articles (Form 2) through BC Registry Online. Provide registered office address, directors' consents (Form 14), and share structure. Pay filing fee by credit card or electronic debit.
required_dossiers: Form 14 – Consent to Act as Director
Directors' addresses and optional passport copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Registrar rejects, correct deficient fields, pay resubmission fee if any, and refile within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation under s. 12 of the BC Business Corporations Act. The company comes into existence on the date of the certificate. Retain certified copy and file annual reports thereafter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request administrative correction if certificate contains clerical error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Combined Business Registration; BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number (BN) via CRA's Business Registration Online. Register for GST/HST, corporate income tax, and BC provincial sales tax (PST). Open a payroll account if employees are hired. Register with WorksafeBC for occupational injury insurance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries, provide clarifications and amend registration via Business Registration Online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the MSB Registration form (FINTRAC form) within 30 days of business commencement. Provide corporate identity, ownership details, compliance program narrative, and AML/ATF policies. Pay statutory fee if applicable (currently C$50).
required_dossiers: Business model and payment rail flowchart
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration incomplete, FINTRAC issues deficiency notice; respond within 30 days and submit revised documentation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; federal business registration and GST/HST administration via Business Registration Online and My Business Account (www.canada.ca); British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax is administered separately by the BC Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch, via eTaxBC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A BC ULC obtains its CRA Business Number (BN) upon corporate creation or by filing Form RC1, Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts. The BN is the statutory Canadian tax ID; separate program accounts are added for corporate income tax (RC), GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP), and customs (RM). A GST/HST registration must be made once the ULC is not a small supplier, i.e. when total taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or over the preceding four calendar quarters; voluntary registration is available under section 240 of the Excise Tax Act. A foreign non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada uses the same Form RC1 process and must provide its foreign corporate registration, principal place of business, authorized Canadian agent, and expected Canadian revenue. For BC PST, the ULC must register separately as a PST seller if it makes taxable sales in BC; no PST registration exemption is generally available merely because the entity is non-resident.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no federal check-the-box regime; a BC ULC is statutorily taxed as a resident corporation on its worldwide income under the Income Tax Act. The pass-through eligibility arises under U.S. federal tax law: a Canadian unlimited liability company is not a per se corporation and may elect classification as a disregarded entity or partnership on IRS Form 8832. Canadian anti-hybrid rules under the Income Tax Act, BEPS Action 2, and the Canada-US tax treaty must be assessed because a ULC can be treated as opaque for Canadian tax and flow-through for U.S. tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST), a value-added tax, combined with British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST), a retail sales tax; together a blended 12% headline consumption tax rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter or across four consecutive calendar quarters for GST/HST (small-supplier exemptions; zero-rated supplies count as taxable supplies). BC PST has no comparable small-supplier threshold; a seller becomes liable to register once it makes taxable retail sales in BC, regardless of turnover volume.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal mandatory electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, or digital tax stamping exists in Canada. CRA operates a self-assessment model; returns and records may be filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE and registered accounts. BC PST also operates without digital invoice clearance. Invoices and records must nevertheless be complete, legible, and available in English or French to satisfy audit requirements; no government API pre-clearance of individual invoices is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Excise Tax Act, goods physically exported by the ULC are zero-rated if the sale is made in the course of the ULC's commercial activity and proof of export is retained. Services are zero-rated where supplied to a non-resident and the service is not rendered to an individual present in Canada and does not relate to real property or tangible goods situated in Canada. For the cross-border remittance rail, fees and settlement charges invoiced to a non-resident financial institution or foreign counterparty for SWIFT/MT202 clearing and cash-pickup settlement may qualify for 0% GST/HST. A fee charged to a Canadian-resident sender for a remittance payout abroad is a Canadian-supplied financial service and does not qualify for zero-rating. BC PST generally does not apply to exported goods or to financial services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A) or Canada Export Declaration (CAED) for any goods movement
Commercial invoice and cross-border money transmission service agreement
Bill of Lading, air waybill, carrier certificate, or customs entry evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign bank statement proving foreign receipt
SWIFT MT103 or MT202 clearing records and foreign correspondent settlement confirmations
KYC/AML files and transaction monitoring records for the remittance rail
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits zero-rating claims requiring documentation within 180 days of the transaction. Insufficient substantiation will cause reversal of the 0% rate, reassessment at 5% GST or 12% GST/PST as applicable, denial or clawback of input tax credits and refunds, arrears interest, and civil penalties for false statements or gross negligence. Deliberate export fraud may lead to criminal tax evasion proceedings under the Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act. Because the BC ULC carries unlimited liability, shareholders cannot rely on corporate limited-liability protection; CRA and BC Ministry of Finance debt, penalties, and interest may be enforced against shareholder assets.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential oversight and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/ATF supervision; Canada maintains no dedicated foreign exchange control administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully liberalized capital account. There is no general foreign exchange control legislation restricting capital or current account convertibility; the Canadian dollar is freely convertible. Profit remittances from a British Columbia Unlimited Liability Corporation (BC ULC), including dividends, interest, and management fees, require no Bank of Canada authorization. Regulatory friction arises only under FINTRAC reporting thresholds (CAD 10,000 or more) and non-resident withholding tax obligations under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada), which can be reduced under applicable tax treaties. The remittance agency must also ensure compliance with MSB-specific FINTRAC record-keeping, registration, and reporting duties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory repatriation ratio applies in Canada. For services export and money transmission, there is no requirement to convert foreign currency receipts into CAD. However, all cross-border transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported by financial intermediaries to FINTRAC. The Bank of Canada and Statistics Canada compile balance-of-payments data requiring reporting by resident banks, not directly by the remittance MSB. Accordingly, the BC ULC may hold foreign currency accounts with Schedule I banks without conversion or surrender requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with material legal constraints. Offshore FinTech Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) can be used only as auxiliary clearing bridges, not as primary custodians of Canadian client funds. Any EMI intending to conduct money transmission in Canada must independently register as a money services business with FINTRAC and, where applicable, obtain a licence under the British Columbia Money Services Business Act. Canadian Schedule I banks routinely apply de-risking policies that reject unregulated offshore EMIs as correspondent settlement partners. Therefore, the primary liquidity clearing rail must be a Canadian Tier 1 bank; the offshore EMI may serve as a technical FX conversion overlay or sub-agent for cash pickup corridors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed high-risk MSB ULC, a physical onboarding interview is effectively mandatory. At least one director or senior officer with signing authority must appear in person at a Vancouver or Toronto branch of the selected bank to complete identity verification and explain the business model. Remote electronic onboarding is available only in exceptionally low-risk scenarios or where the bank already has a substantial relationship. Non-resident directors may be required to attend a Canadian consular verification or submit a notarized identity dossier with a corresponding bank reference and certified corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited liability company structure combined with non-resident beneficial owners and pass-through tax classification appears to undermine shareholder accountability and create potential abuse of the unlimited liability wrapper.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC Registry certificate of good standing, notice of articles and full constitutional deed, legal opinion on ULC idiosyncrasies under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), Canadian federal tax classification letter or legal memorandum confirming the pass-through election, executed beneficial ownership schedule identifying each individual owner, and an independent corporate background screening report from a reputable international advisory firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk money services business license flag due to cross-border remittance corridors, cash-pickup payout networks, and high transaction velocity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid FINTRAC MSB registration certificate, BC Money Services Business Act licence or evidence of application in process, comprehensive AML/ATF compliance manual tailored to the operation, enterprise-wide risk assessment and product risk matrix, executed agency and correspondent agreements, evidence of transaction monitoring platform implementation, and audited financial projections prepared by a licensed Canadian CPA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large volume of low-value inbound transfers commingled with operating funds creates suspicion of layering, fragmentation, and unregistered money transmission.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business model documentation including end-to-end payment flow diagrams, sample transaction chain from sender initiation to overseas cash payout, segregation of client funds in trust and operational accounts, formal liquidity risk policy, and a two-year external AML audit report confirming monitoring thresholds and suspicious transaction reporting procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening concerns arising from payout corridors touching United States OFAC-listed jurisdictions or high-risk regional payment partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time sanctions screening policy incorporating the Canadian Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act regulations, and OFAC SDN list; independent penetration testing report confirming filter calibration; contractual documentation that the remittance agency does not service sanctioned persons or jurisdictions; legal opinion validating the sanctions filter and escalation protocol.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived lack of Canadian physical substance due to reliance on offshore EMI infrastructure and remote management.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consolidated banking relationship confirmation with a Schedule I bank, signed agreement showing the offshore EMI acts solely as a technical processor without possession of Canadian client funds, EMI's home jurisdiction regulatory licence and good standing certificate, Canadian legal analysis of extraterritorial applicability of EMI licensing, and a de-risking mitigation strategy including a Canadian resident compliance officer appointment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital injections are routed through SWIFT MT103 beneficiary-set to the BC ULC's trust account with a Canadian Schedule I clearing bank. The remitting institution must include purpose code 105 'Remittance of own capital' or a Shareholder Loan purpose code in SWIFT field 70; the Canadian beneficiary bank will validate the corporate name, UBI number, and settlement account number. For FX compliance, the inbound transfer is settled via the Canadian Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for CAD liquidity or SWIFT gpi for foreign currency. Verification includes daily treasury reconciliation against bank statements, FINTRAC suspicious transaction screening, and documentation of the source of funds including board-approved capital subscription agreement and director KYC.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and customer disbursements use SWIFT MT103 single-credit transfers with mandatory SWIFT gpi tracking; for higher-value agency payments, commercial Letters of Credit (LC) are opened through the settling Canadian bank. The domestic leg of any CAD disbursement clears through LVTS, with US dollar disbursements routed through the corresponding bank's USD clearing in New York and EUR disbursements through SWIFT EUR-TARGET. For cash-pickup corridors in lower banking penetration countries, the BC ULC instructs the Canadian bank to send a cover payment (MT202COV) to a local partner bank, with FX conversion occurring at the local partner bank's daily reference rate. All transfer instructions include legal entity identifiers and detailed remittance purpose codes to prevent anti-money laundering false positives.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX Call and Put Options (when executed with an OSFI-supervised dealer)

stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide BN and the corporation's Canadian mailing address; the ULC files as a Canadian-resident corporation even when all shareholders are non-residents; attach the completed provincial BC tax schedule.
